# Template catalog

<!-- Generated by scripts/generate-docs.mjs from the template registry. Do not edit by hand. -->

Every scene names one template in `primitive.template` and fills its
slots in `primitive.content`. These are the 35 templates
that ship with `@lenzon/player`, version-matched to this package.

The first 16 suit any idea: a business plan, a process, a
concept. The other 19 only make sense for software, such as
a diff or a pull request.

Slots marked optional, or with a default, can be left out. A beat's
`emphasize` target is different for each template, so each entry says
what it takes.

For how to write a good script, read `WRITING-SCRIPTS.md` beside this file.

## For any idea

- [`center-stage`](#center-stage): Central concept on canvas in Instrument Serif italic with related terms orbiting around it.
- [`code-cloud`](#code-cloud): Weighted DOM word cloud for concepts inside a glass plate.
- [`compare-split`](#compare-split): Side-by-side comparison of two parallel options inside glass plates with a divider.
- [`constraint-wall`](#constraint-wall): The "what we refused to do" beat of a series explainer: constraint objectives rendered as a wall of deliberate refusals, each card carrying a WON'T mark, the statement, an optional PR ref, and an optional evidence line.
- [`decision-ledger`](#decision-ledger): A plan's decisions, each marked settled, chosen, rejected or open.
- [`emphasis-word`](#emphasis-word): Large dramatic word on canvas in Instrument Serif italic with optional mono eyebrow subtitle.
- [`entity-map`](#entity-map): Friendly ER diagram in nested glass plates: model cards with fields, connected by labeled relationship lines.
- [`flow-diagram`](#flow-diagram): Directed graph of labeled nodes and edges, rendered as scalable SVG with staggered entrance.
- [`purpose-bullets`](#purpose-bullets): Purpose statement on canvas with typed supporting evidence in a glass plate.
- [`risk-matrix`](#risk-matrix): Triage 2×2 plot for gotchas — impact × likelihood.
- [`roadmap-rail`](#roadmap-rail): A roadmap as one road wider than the stage.
- [`scorecard`](#scorecard): Report card grid with a large overall letter grade and per-metric severity bars inside glass plates.
- [`sequence-diagram`](#sequence-diagram): UML sequence diagram: actor lanes across the top, animated arrows between them showing who calls whom and in what order.
- [`step-journey`](#step-journey): Horizontal step-by-step journey with numbered circles, labels, and a connecting progress line.
- [`title-bullets`](#title-bullets): Canvas title in Instrument Serif italic with a staggered DOM numbered list in a glass plate below.
- [`transform-grid`](#transform-grid): Horizontal pipeline of stages in nested glass plates that reveal left-to-right with connector glyphs.

## For code

- [`code-diff`](#code-diff): Before/after view of a hunk.
- [`code-zoom`](#code-zoom): Code block in a sunken glass plate that zooms in from small, with optional line highlighting and warm pulse.
- [`component-impact`](#component-impact): Relative impact of each component across a series, as a rotating isometric city: a muted baseline volume with the series' change stacked on top in accent.
- [`data-pipeline`](#data-pipeline): Animated data transformation pipeline showing actual values flowing through stacked sunken glass cards (map, filter, reduce, etc.).
- [`delivery-steps`](#delivery-steps): The PRs that built a planning doc, drawn as a staircase climbing to the doc itself: each step a card saying what that PR added, with its number, title and analyzed date.
- [`directory-tree`](#directory-tree): Repository/directory structure view inside a glass plate.
- [`drift-callout`](#drift-callout): Beat 4 of a spec explainer: where the code moved away from the spec since it was last grounded.
- [`era-timeline`](#era-timeline): The spine of a series explainer: a dated horizontal axis with one tick per PR, grouped into labelled era bands coloured by dominant area.
- [`file-trajectory`](#file-trajectory): One file and its life across a series: every touch in order, each with the analyst's own description, on a vertical spine with PR ref and date.
- [`objective-ledger`](#objective-ledger): The "what got done" beat of a series explainer: objectives from many PRs rolled into one ledger, grouped by era, each line attributed to its PR and coloured by kind (primary / secondary / constraint).
- [`outro-card`](#outro-card): Closing slide of a PR-explainer run.
- [`plan-title-card`](#plan-title-card): Opening slide of a spec-explainer run — one planning doc rather than a PR.
- [`pr-objectives`](#pr-objectives): Frames what a PR is trying to do as three visually distinct tiers: 1–2 primary (largest), 0–4 secondary (medium), 0–3 constraints (smaller, dim, 'WON'T' framing).
- [`pr-title-card`](#pr-title-card): Opening slide of a PR-explainer run.
- [`repo-pulse`](#repo-pulse): Community/liveness card: activity signal badge, commit-recency stats, contributor counts, and top contributors.
- [`review-priority-matrix`](#review-priority-matrix): Reading plan for a series under one lens — a 2×2 of impact × review-worthiness with one dot per PR.
- [`series-title-card`](#series-title-card): Opening slide of a series-explainer run — a stretch of work rather than one PR.
- [`tech-stack-breakdown`](#tech-stack-breakdown): Full-bleed grid breaking the repo tech stack into optional standard categories: Network, Data, Application, Services, UI, DevOps.
- [`title-card`](#title-card): Opening slide of an analysis: a single full-bleed glass plate with a kicker, org/repo display headline, optional blurb, and a meta footer (analysis date, commit · branch).

## For any idea, in detail

### center-stage

Central concept on canvas in Instrument Serif italic with related terms orbiting around it. Weight drives size and ink brightness.

Content slots:

- `center`: { text: string, size?: number } — the central concept
- `orbiting`: { text: string, weight: number }[] — satellite terms (weight 0-1). Use 4–6 terms of one short word each. Terms are sized by weight alone and never measured, so two-word terms, or weights above 0.7 on long words, overlap each other and the center
- `staggerMs`: number — delay between orbiter entrances (default 200)
- `orbitSpeed`: number — radians/frame for slow rotation (default 0 = static)
- `centerFx`: EffectSpec[] — entrance effects for the center word

Emphasize target: an orbiting term, by 0-based index or by its text.

Example `primitive`:

```json
{
  "template": "center-stage",
  "content": {
    "center": {"text":"Presenter","size":144},
    "orbiting": [
      {"text":"Stage","weight":0.9},
      {"text":"TextBox","weight":0.8},
      {"text":"fx registry","weight":0.7},
      {"text":"Templates","weight":0.85},
      {"text":"DOM Layer","weight":0.6},
      {"text":"Stage3D","weight":0.3}
    ],
    "staggerMs": 200
  }
}
```

Example beat: `{"at":2,"action":{"type":"emphasize","target":"Templates"}}`

### code-cloud

Weighted DOM word cloud for concepts inside a glass plate. Scatter / spiral / typewriter entrance; gentle float after placement (opt-in).

Content slots:

- `items`: { text: string, weight: number, category: string }[] — cloud items
- `categoryColors`: Record<string, string> — category → color (CSS, var(--cs-*), or palette.* alias)
- `entranceStyle`: "scatter" | "spiral" | "typewriter" — how items appear
- `float`: boolean — opt-in continuous gentle float after entrance (default false)

Emphasize target: an item, by its text, in any case.

Example `primitive`:

```json
{
  "template": "code-cloud",
  "content": {
    "items": [
      {"text":"React","weight":1,"category":"framework"},
      {"text":"Express","weight":0.9,"category":"framework"},
      {"text":"useState","weight":0.85,"category":"pattern"},
      {"text":"prisma","weight":0.7,"category":"orm"},
      {"text":"JWT","weight":0.6,"category":"auth"},
      {"text":"WebSocket","weight":0.4,"category":"transport"},
      {"text":"Redis","weight":0.3,"category":"cache"},
      {"text":"useEffect","weight":0.75,"category":"pattern"},
      {"text":"Postgres","weight":0.65,"category":"orm"}
    ],
    "categoryColors": {
      "framework": "var(--cs-accent-cool)",
      "pattern": "var(--cs-ink-1)",
      "orm": "var(--cs-accent-ok)",
      "auth": "var(--cs-accent-warn)",
      "transport": "var(--cs-ink-2)",
      "cache": "var(--cs-ink-3)"
    },
    "entranceStyle": "spiral"
  }
}
```

Example beat: `{"at":2,"action":{"type":"emphasize","target":"JWT"}}`

### compare-split

Side-by-side comparison of two parallel options inside glass plates with a divider. For mode contrasts, analogies, tradeoffs, before/after. Prefer it over transform-grid when the two things are alternatives rather than steps.

Content slots:

- `title`: string — optional headline above the comparison
- `left`: { heading, icon?, bullets?, accent? } — left panel. accent is a CSS color or palette.primary|secondary|accent
- `right`: { heading, icon?, bullets?, accent? } — right panel
- `divider`: "vs" | "or" | "→" | "none" (default "vs"; use "→" for before/after)
- `staggerMs`: number — delay between reveals (default 400)
- `chosen`: "left" | "right" — optional; the side a decision picked. Moves the accent there and quiets the other side

Emphasize target: "left" or "right".

Example `primitive`:

```json
{
  "template": "compare-split",
  "content": {
    "title": "Two Ways to Use It",
    "left": {
      "heading": "Tag Mode",
      "icon": "Interactive",
      "bullets": [
        "Invoked with @claude in comments",
        "Full PR context at its disposal",
        "Can push commits back to the branch"
      ],
      "accent": "palette.primary"
    },
    "right": {
      "heading": "Agent Mode",
      "icon": "Automated",
      "bullets": [
        "Driven by a custom prompt",
        "Runs on a schedule or trigger",
        "Produces structured output"
      ],
      "accent": "palette.secondary"
    },
    "divider": "vs",
    "staggerMs": 400
  }
}
```

Example beat: `{"at":2,"action":{"type":"emphasize","target":"right"}}`

### constraint-wall

The "what we refused to do" beat of a series explainer: constraint objectives rendered as a wall of deliberate refusals, each card carrying a WON'T mark, the statement, an optional PR ref, and an optional evidence line. Built for the case where evidence is absent by nature — a constraint describes something that was not done — so cards with no citation read as intentional rather than incomplete.

Content slots:

- `heading`: string — optional headline (default "What this work refused to do")
- `items`: { statement, prNumber?, evidence? }[] — the refusals; evidence is legitimately absent on most constraints and is simply omitted, never placeholdered
- `tone`: 'stated' | 'dim' — full-contrast claim (default) vs a quieter background wall under narration
- `staggerMs`: number — total card reveal window (default 1000)

Emphasize target: a card by 0-based index ("item:2" or "2"), or "pr:<number>" for every card from that PR.

Example `primitive`:

```json
{
  "template": "constraint-wall",
  "content": {
    "heading": "What this work refused to do",
    "tone": "stated",
    "items": [
      {
        "statement": "Preserve Analysis as the authoritative source; the index remains a cache",
        "prNumber": 21,
        "evidence": "apps/server/lib/corpus/queries.ts"
      },
      {
        "statement": "Refuse checks with unjoinable inputs rather than reporting empty results",
        "prNumber": 26,
        "evidence": "packages/sidecar/src/validate.ts"
      },
      {
        "statement": "Preserve \"no snapshot\" as distinct from empty or zero counts",
        "prNumber": 33
      },
      {
        "statement": "No invented numbers — every count the narration states is computed upstream",
        "prNumber": 21
      },
      {
        "statement": "Keep templates calm by default; continuous motion stays opt-in",
        "prNumber": 16
      },
      {"statement":"No database migrations in this stretch","prNumber":17}
    ],
    "staggerMs": 1000
  }
}
```

Example beat: `{"at":2,"action":{"type":"emphasize","target":"item:2"}}`

### decision-ledger

A plan's decisions, each marked settled, chosen, rejected or open. Settled, chosen and rejected rows may carry a date and a one-line why; open rows carry nothing extra. The header counts rows by state. Refs render as written, without "#".

Content slots:

- `title`: string — optional headline (default "Where the decisions stand")
- `decisions`: { ref?, question, state: 'settled'|'chosen'|'rejected'|'open', date?, why? }[] — in doc order; date and why are dropped on open rows
- `staggerMs`: number — total row reveal window (default 900)

Emphasize target: a row by 0-based index ("2" or "item:2"), or "state:<state>" for every row in that state, such as "state:open".

Example `primitive`:

```json
{
  "template": "decision-ledger",
  "content": {
    "title": "The planning doctrine: what is decided",
    "decisions": [
      {
        "ref": "§8.1",
        "question": "May an agent prose-edit an L3 specification?",
        "state": "open"
      },
      {
        "ref": "§8.2",
        "question": "Does reference become a fourth category, or fold into L1?",
        "state": "open"
      },
      {
        "ref": "§8.3",
        "question": "Where do specs live on disk?",
        "state": "open"
      },
      {
        "ref": "§8.4",
        "question": "Should landed be refused on canonical docs?",
        "state": "open",
        "date": "2026-08-20",
        "why": "Dropped by the template: an open row carries nothing extra."
      },
      {
        "ref": "§8.5",
        "question": "Do L1 docs opt out of implementation drift?",
        "state": "settled",
        "date": "2026-08-29",
        "why": "No. Drift is still measured; acting on it is the author’s call."
      },
      {
        "ref": "§8.7",
        "question": "Do lenzon-ui-concept and sidecar-human-legibility become children of this doc?",
        "state": "open"
      }
    ],
    "staggerMs": 900
  }
}
```

Example beat: `{"at":2,"action":{"type":"emphasize","target":"4"}}`

### emphasis-word

Large dramatic word on canvas in Instrument Serif italic with optional mono eyebrow subtitle. Built for verdict statements and key reveals.

Content slots:

- `word`: string — the headline word or short phrase
- `subtitle`: string — optional supporting text that fades in below
- `fx`: EffectSpec[] — entrance effects (defaults to slam + warm glow)
- `style`: { size?: number, weight?: string, color?: string } — optional overrides

Emphasize target: any target. It glows the word again.

Example `primitive`:

```json
{
  "template": "emphasis-word",
  "content": {
    "word": "FRAGILE",
    "subtitle": "This codebase has no tests and 3 god functions over 500 lines each."
  }
}
```

### entity-map

Friendly ER diagram in nested glass plates: model cards with fields, connected by labeled relationship lines.

Content slots:

- `title`: string — optional headline
- `entities`: { id, label, fields?, color?, row?, col? }[] — the models/tables (3–10). row/col are 1-indexed grid coords; omit to auto-pack. Every entity should appear in at least one relationship, since a lone card reads as an error. Trim the list rather than invent links.
- `relationships`: { from, to, label, type? }[] — connections between entities. from/to MUST match an entity id, or the line is dropped. label is plain English ("has many", "owns"), not database notation. type (one-to-one|one-to-many|many-to-one|many-to-many) draws the 1/N marks
- `staggerMs`: number — delay between card reveals (default 300)
- `layout`: "grid" | "hierarchical" — layout strategy (default "grid")

Emphasize target: an entity id. It pulses the card and lights its relationship lines.

Example `primitive`:

```json
{
  "template": "entity-map",
  "content": {
    "title": "Data model at a glance",
    "entities": [
      {
        "id": "org",
        "label": "Organization",
        "fields": ["id","name","plan"],
        "row": 1,
        "col": 1
      },
      {
        "id": "user",
        "label": "User",
        "fields": ["id","email","name"],
        "row": 1,
        "col": 2
      },
      {
        "id": "project",
        "label": "Project",
        "fields": ["id","name","orgId"],
        "row": 2,
        "col": 1
      },
      {
        "id": "presentation",
        "label": "Presentation",
        "fields": ["id","projectId","script"],
        "row": 2,
        "col": 2
      }
    ],
    "relationships": [
      {"from":"org","to":"user","label":"has many","type":"one-to-many"},
      {"from":"org","to":"project","label":"has many","type":"one-to-many"},
      {
        "from": "project",
        "to": "presentation",
        "label": "has many",
        "type": "one-to-many"
      }
    ],
    "staggerMs": 300
  }
}
```

Example beat: `{"at":2,"action":{"type":"emphasize","target":"project"}}`

### flow-diagram

Directed graph of labeled nodes and edges, rendered as scalable SVG with staggered entrance. Good for architecture and data flow.

Content slots:

- `nodes`: { id, label, group? }[] — nodes in the graph
- `edges`: { from, to, label? }[] — directed edges
- `groups`: { id, label, color }[] — optional node groups (color = CSS or palette.*)
- `staggerMs`: number — delay between node entrances (default 250)
- `layout`: "left-to-right" | "top-to-bottom" | "radial"
- `orbit`: boolean — accepted for back-compat; no-op in the SVG renderer

Emphasize target: a node id.

Example `primitive`:

```json
{
  "template": "flow-diagram",
  "content": {
    "nodes": [
      {"id":"client","label":"Browser","group":"frontend"},
      {"id":"api","label":"API Server","group":"backend"},
      {"id":"auth","label":"Auth Service","group":"backend"},
      {"id":"db","label":"PostgreSQL","group":"data"}
    ],
    "edges": [
      {"from":"client","to":"api","label":"REST"},
      {"from":"api","to":"auth","label":"verify token"},
      {"from":"api","to":"db","label":"queries"}
    ],
    "groups": [
      {"id":"frontend","label":"Frontend","color":"palette.primary"},
      {"id":"backend","label":"Backend","color":"palette.secondary"},
      {"id":"data","label":"Data Layer","color":"palette.accent"}
    ],
    "staggerMs": 300,
    "layout": "left-to-right"
  }
}
```

Example beat: `{"at":2,"action":{"type":"emphasize","target":"auth"}}`

### purpose-bullets

Purpose statement on canvas with typed supporting evidence in a glass plate. File reference badge optional.

Content slots:

- `purpose`: string — the main purpose headline, rendered on canvas. A tagline of 3–5 words, about 25 characters, so it fits on one line. It is drawn at a fixed 96px, so a longer one wraps, and on a small stage its top line is cut off. Detail belongs in supports
- `fileRef`: string — optional file path shown as a badge
- `supports`: SupportItem[] — { point: string, type: feature|detail|concern|strength }
- `purposeFx`: EffectSpec[] — optional entrance effects for the purpose text

Emphasize target: a support point, by 0-based index or by a piece of its text.

Example `primitive`:

```json
{
  "template": "purpose-bullets",
  "content": {
    "purpose": "Handles user authentication and sessions",
    "fileRef": "src/services/auth.ts",
    "supports": [
      {
        "point": "OAuth2 flow with Google and GitHub providers",
        "type": "feature"
      },
      {"point":"JWT tokens with 24-hour expiry","type":"detail"},
      {
        "point": "No refresh token rotation — sessions die on expiry",
        "type": "concern"
      },
      {
        "point": "Rate limiting on login attempts (good practice)",
        "type": "strength"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Example beat: `{"at":2,"action":{"type":"emphasize","target":"2"}}`

### risk-matrix

Triage 2×2 plot for gotchas — impact × likelihood. Each risk renders as an ID-badged dot at (likelihood, impact); colliding dots auto-nudge. Optional faint quadrant labels ("Address first" / "Monitor" / "Fix soon" / "Acceptable") in the corners. Dots stagger in on mount; emphasize(id) pulses one risk.

Content slots:

- `title`: string — optional headline (default "Risks identified")
- `xAxis`: { label?, low?, high? } — defaults likelihood, "rare"/"likely"
- `yAxis`: { label?, low?, high? } — defaults impact, "low"/"high"
- `items`: RiskItem[] — { id, label, impact 0-1, likelihood 0-1, file?, lineRange? }
- `quadrantLabels`: { topRight?, topLeft?, bottomRight?, bottomLeft? } — faint corner text
- `staggerMs`: number — between-dot reveal delay (default 220)

Emphasize target: a risk id to pulse it. "reveal:<id>" shows it.

Example `primitive`:

```json
{
  "template": "risk-matrix",
  "content": {
    "title": "Risks identified",
    "xAxis": {"label":"Likelihood","low":"Rare","high":"Likely"},
    "yAxis": {"label":"Impact","low":"Low","high":"High"},
    "items": [
      {
        "id": "R1",
        "label": "Realpath cache miss",
        "impact": 0.72,
        "likelihood": 0.55,
        "file": "src/upload/path-validator.ts",
        "lineRange": "L42-L51"
      },
      {
        "id": "R2",
        "label": "Symlink outside ROOT slips through on Windows",
        "impact": 0.85,
        "likelihood": 0.22,
        "file": "src/upload/path-validator.ts",
        "lineRange": "L60-L72"
      },
      {
        "id": "R3",
        "label": "Error message leaks server paths",
        "impact": 0.28,
        "likelihood": 0.45,
        "file": "src/upload/errors.ts",
        "lineRange": "L8-L14"
      }
    ],
    "quadrantLabels": {
      "topRight": "Address first",
      "topLeft": "Monitor",
      "bottomRight": "Fix soon",
      "bottomLeft": "Acceptable"
    },
    "staggerMs": 240
  }
}
```

Example beat: `{"at":2,"action":{"type":"emphasize","target":"R1"}}`

### roadmap-rail

A roadmap as one road wider than the stage. Sign posts carry a status; each beat pans to a post and the pan holds.

Content slots:

- `title`: string — the roadmap’s name
- `stretches`: { id, label }[] — tiers or phases, in road order
- `posts`: { label, stretch, status: "landed"|"active"|"parked"|"not-started"|null, detail?, date? }[] — in road order. null status draws as unknown
- `currentPost`: number — index of the "you are here" post. Omit when the source names none

Emphasize target: a post, by 0-based index. The road pans to centre it, and it pulses.

Example `primitive`:

```json
{
  "template": "roadmap-rail",
  "content": {
    "title": "Roadmap — Community Signal",
    "stretches": [
      {"id":"built","label":"Already a capability"},
      {"id":"tier-1","label":"Tier 1 — Sharpens the demand test"},
      {"id":"tier-2","label":"Tier 2 — Differentiators"},
      {"id":"tier-3","label":"Tier 3 — Parked"}
    ],
    "posts": [
      {"label":"Structured risk pass","stretch":"built","status":"landed"},
      {"label":"Examined vs found","stretch":"built","status":"landed"},
      {"label":"Standards lens","stretch":"built","status":"landed"},
      {
        "label": "Cost gating by size",
        "stretch": "tier-1",
        "status": "not-started"
      },
      {
        "label": "Strip noisy files",
        "stretch": "tier-1",
        "status": "not-started"
      },
      {
        "label": "Fail silent",
        "stretch": "tier-1",
        "status": "not-started",
        "detail": "Failed runs still show a red check"
      },
      {"label":"Anti-batching line","stretch":"tier-1","status":"landed"},
      {
        "label": "High-signal explaining",
        "stretch": "tier-2",
        "status": "not-started"
      },
      {"label":"Author tracking","stretch":"tier-2","status":"not-started"},
      {
        "label": "Config UI",
        "stretch": "tier-2",
        "status": "active",
        "detail": "Lens workbench, in design"
      },
      {"label":"Merge gating","stretch":"tier-3","status":"parked"},
      {"label":"Autonomous action","stretch":"tier-3","status":"parked"},
      {"label":"Prescriptive verdicts","stretch":"tier-3","status":"parked"},
      {"label":"Lint-test-AI gate","stretch":"tier-3","status":"parked"},
      {
        "label": "Correctness guarantees",
        "stretch": "tier-3",
        "status": "parked"
      },
      {"label":"Slack and chat","stretch":"tier-3","status":"parked"}
    ],
    "currentPost": 9
  }
}
```

### scorecard

Report card grid with a large overall letter grade and per-metric severity bars inside glass plates.

Content slots:

- `title`: string — optional headline
- `overallGrade`: string — overall letter grade (A through F)
- `items`: { label, grade, note }[] — individual scored metrics (3–8)

Emphasize target: an item, by 0-based index.

Example `primitive`:

```json
{
  "template": "scorecard",
  "content": {
    "title": "Codebase report card",
    "overallGrade": "C+",
    "items": [
      {
        "label": "Architecture",
        "grade": "B+",
        "note": "Clean layering, clear seams."
      },
      {"label":"Testing","grade":"F","note":"No tests at all."},
      {
        "label": "Security",
        "grade": "C-",
        "note": "JWTs are not signature-verified."
      },
      {"label":"Docs","grade":"B","note":"README + inline is solid."},
      {"label":"Performance","grade":"A-","note":"Async, cached, indexed."},
      {"label":"Dependencies","grade":"C","note":"2 majors behind latest."}
    ]
  }
}
```

Example beat: `{"at":2,"action":{"type":"emphasize","target":"1"}}`

### sequence-diagram

UML sequence diagram: actor lanes across the top, animated arrows between them showing who calls whom and in what order.

Content slots:

- `title`: string — optional headline
- `actors`: { id, label }[] — up to ~5 lanes
- `steps`: { from, to, label, kind: "request"|"response"|"self"|"note" }[]
- `staggerMs`: number — delay between arrow reveals (default 700)

Emphasize target: a step, by 0-based index, or an actor id.

Example `primitive`:

```json
{
  "template": "sequence-diagram",
  "content": {
```

## For code, in detail

### code-diff

Before/after view of a hunk. Split mode renders two columns side by side (preferred when line correspondence matters); unified mode renders one column with +/− gutters. Bilateral line highlighting via emphasize("before:N" | "after:N" | "pair:N").

Content slots:

- `file`: string — file path shown as a badge above the diff
- `language`: string — prism language id (default: "javascript")
- `mode`: "split" | "unified" — column layout (default "split")
- `before`: { code, startLine?, highlight? } — original side
- `after`: { code, startLine?, highlight? } — replacement side
- `caption`: string — optional 1-line summary below the diff
- `startScale`: number — initial zoom scale (default 0.15)

Emphasize target: "before:N", "after:N" or "pair:N" lights line N on one side or both, and stays lit. "before" or "after" pulses a whole side. "clear" resets.

Example `primitive`:

```json
{
  "template": "code-diff",
  "content": {
    "file": "src/upload/path-validator.ts",
    "language": "typescript",
    "mode": "split",
    "before": {
      "code": "function validatePath(p: string) {\n  if (p.includes('..')) {\n    throw new Error('escape');\n  }\n  return p;\n}",
      "startLine": 40,
      "highlight": [42]
    },
    "after": {
      "code": "function validatePath(p: string) {\n  const real = realpathSync(p);\n  if (!real.startsWith(ROOT)) {\n    throw new PathEscapeError(p);\n  }\n  return real;\n}",
      "startLine": 40,
      "highlight": [42,43]
    },
    "caption": "realpath + prefix check replaces the substring test",
    "startScale": 0.15
  }
}
```

### component-impact

Relative impact of each component across a series, as a rotating isometric city: a muted baseline volume with the series' change stacked on top in accent. One bounded rotation establishes depth, then the change volumes grow — growth is the producer's emphasis hook, so the change lands on a narration beat. Height is linear in a named unit and never rescaled per block, so equal heights mean equal magnitude.

Content slots:

- `title`: string — optional headline (default "Where the work landed")
- `blocks`: { id, label, baseline, change, district? }[] — one per component; baseline 0 marks a component created during the window
- `unitLabel`: string — what baseline/change count ("lines", "touches", "PRs"); rendered in the legend because a bare number is not a fact
- `maxBlocks`: number — keep the N largest-change blocks; the remainder is disclosed as a count and a combined change total
- `baselineLabel`: string — legend word for the muted volume (default "baseline")
- `changeLabel`: string — legend word for the accent volume (default "changed this window")
- `markNew`: boolean — mark baseline-0 blocks NEW (default true); false when baseline 0 does not mean "created in the window"
- `fromAngle`: number — yaw degrees the rotation starts from (default 8)
- `toAngle`: number — yaw degrees it settles at (default 30)
- `growthMode`: 'on-emphasis' (default) — change volumes wait for a beat; 'auto' — they grow once after the rotation
- `rotateMs`: number — rotation duration (default 1400)
- `growMs`: number — per-block growth duration (default 900)

Emphasize target: "grow" grows every change volume, and is the main beat. "grow:<id>" grows one. "<id>" pulses a block and grows it. "district:<name>" pulses a district. "reset" collapses them.

Example `primitive`:

### data-pipeline

Animated data transformation pipeline showing actual values flowing through stacked sunken glass cards (map, filter, reduce, etc.).

Content slots:

- `title`: string — optional headline
- `input`: { label, data, display? } — the starting data
- `stages`: { operation, label, result, highlight?, display? }[] — transformation stages (2–5); display is "table" | "value" | "breakdown"
- `staggerMs`: number — delay between stage reveals (default 1500)

Emphasize target: a stage, by 0-based index. The input is not a stage, so "0" is the first transformation.

```json
        "highlight": "total",
```

### delivery-steps

The PRs that built a planning doc, drawn as a staircase climbing to the doc itself: each step a card saying what that PR added, with its number, title and analyzed date. The frontmatter delivered-by list renders apart in a strip below and is never matched to the steps. Long lists collapse from the middle and state how many are not shown.

Content slots:

- `docId`: string — doc id the steps build toward (e.g. "pipeline-spec")
- `title`: string | null — the doc title, shown in the target block
- `level`: "L1" | "L2" | "L3" — shown as a badge in the target block
- `steps`: { prNumber, title, analyzedAt, motivation, objectives[] }[] — oldest first, copied from the digest delivery steps
- `stepsFound`: number — PRs found before any cap; drives the "N of M" chip
- `declared`: (number | string)[] — delivered-by as written; rendered apart, never matched to steps
- `maxSteps`: number — cap on rendered steps (default 6); the middle collapses
- `kicker`: string — small uppercase label above the headline
- `headline`: string — one line on what the steps add up to
- `staggerMs`: number — total step reveal window (default 1200)

Emphasize target: a step by 0-based index, "pr:<n>", "target" or "declared".

Example `primitive`:

```json
{
  "template": "delivery-steps",
  "content": {
    "docId": "pipeline-spec",
    "title": "Lenzon — The Pipeline (Current State)",
    "level": "L3",
    "kicker": "Delivery",
    "headline": "Three PRs built the pipeline this spec describes",

        "paths": [

        "prNumber": 63,
```

### directory-tree

Repository/directory structure view inside a glass plate. For showing how a project is organized, which folders matter. Calm/static after the depth-stagger reveal.

Content slots:

- `root`: string — optional root label shown at the top
- `tree`: TreeNode[] — { name, badge?, note?, highlight?, children? }. A name ending in "/" is a folder, and so is a node with children. badge is short pill text, note a dim caption, highlight an accent stripe
- `maxDepth`: number — collapse deeper levels (default 3)
- `staggerMs`: number — per-depth reveal delay (default 200)
- `style`: "tree" | "indented" | "explorer" (default "tree")

Emphasize target: a full path ("src/utils/auth.ts") or a bare name ("auth.ts").

### drift-callout

Beat 4 of a spec explainer: where the code moved away from the spec since it was last grounded. A gap band (grounded sha and date → drift onset → days since grounding) over a split: the drawing (doc id, title, grounding, an optional quoted claim) and the building (each path changed since grounding with the merges that touched it, plus edited parent docs). Dates and day counts render only as supplied; a skipped merge sweep and any shortened list are disclosed.

Content slots:

- `heading`: string — optional headline (default "Where the code moved")
- `docId`: string — doc id (SpecIdentity.docId)
- `title`: string — the doc title (SpecIdentity.title)
- `relPath`: string — repo-relative path (SpecIdentity.relPath)
- `groundedAt`: string — grounding sha (SpecIdentity.groundedAt)
- `groundedOn`: string — grounding commit date (SpecIdentity.groundedOn)
- `daysSinceGrounding`: number — from the digest; omitted means not shown
- `claim`: string — a short line the spec claims, quoted verbatim
- `onsetAt`: string | null — when drift began (SpecDrift.onsetAt); null = undated
- `changedFiles`: string[] — SpecDrift.changedFiles
- `changedParents`: { id, relPath }[] — SpecDrift.changedParents
- `commits`: string[] — SpecDrift.commits ("sha subject")
- `merges`: { number, sha, subject, mergedAt, changedPaths }[] — SpecDrift.merges
- `mergeSweep`: { swept, reason, truncated } — SpecDrift.mergeSweep
- `maxFiles`: number — file rows before the rest collapse (default 5, or 4 with parents)

Emphasize target: "drawing", "building" or "gap"; a changed file, by path or bare name; or a PR number, "#12" or "12".

Example `primitive`:

```json
{
  "template": "drift-callout",
  "content": {
    "heading": "Where the code moved",
    "docId": "pipeline-spec",
    "title": "Lenzon — The Pipeline (Current State)",
    "relPath": "docs/PIPELINE.md",
    "groundedAt": "c2c8e47",
    "groundedOn": "2026-10-03",
    "daysSinceGrounding": 23,
    "claim": "A PrExplainerRun row is upserted when the webhook lands, then the worker drives the rest.",
    "onsetAt": "2026-10-05",
    "changedFiles": ["apps/server/prisma/schema.prisma"],
    "changedParents": [],
    "commits": [
      "281bd56 Let a person retire a document from its card, with a reason",
      "4320ebc Let a person accept or decline an extraction proposal from the card",
      "2defd2c Let a re-verify verdict replace its button, and colour only Current"
    ],
    "merges": [
      {
        "number": 163,
        "sha": "deaa0d3",
        "subject": "Let a re-verify verdict replace its button, and colour only Current",
        "mergedAt": "2026-10-05",
        "changedPaths": ["apps/server/prisma/schema.prisma"]
      },
      {
        "number": 166,
        "sha": "4588ce0",
        "subject": "Let a person accept or decline an extraction proposal from the card",
        "mergedAt": "2026-10-06",
        "changedPaths": ["apps/server/prisma/schema.prisma"]
      },
      {
        "number": 169,
        "sha": "e9d9d8d",
        "subject": "Let a person retire a document from its card, with a reason",
        "mergedAt": "2026-10-06",
        "changedPaths": ["apps/server/prisma/schema.prisma"]
      }
    ],
    "mergeSweep": {"swept":true,"reason":null,"truncated":false}
  }
}
```

### era-timeline

The spine of a series explainer: a dated horizontal axis with one tick per PR, grouped into labelled era bands coloured by dominant area. Ticks are positioned by date so gaps and clustering carry information; PRs with no analysis render as hollow rings rather than being dropped. Legend lists each era with its PR count and area.

Content slots:

- `title`: string — optional headline (default "How the work moved")
- `eras`: { label, from, to, prCount?, dominantArea?, accent? }[] — labelled bands; accent is palette.primary|secondary|accent or a css color
- `ticks`: { prNumber, at?, title?, weight?, flagged? }[] — one per PR; `at` is an ISO date (positions the tick), `flagged` marks an unanalyzed PR as a hollow ring
- `axis`: { from?, to? } — axis extent; derived from ticks when omitted
- `staggerMs`: number — total tick reveal window (default 900)

Emphasize target: "era:<label>", "pr:<number>" or "axis".

### file-trajectory

One file and its life across a series: every touch in order, each with the analyst's own description, on a vertical spine with PR ref and date. Optional co-change rail lists files that moved alongside it. Long trajectories collapse from the middle and state how many touches are not shown, keeping the first and current touch visible.

Content slots:

- `path`: string — the file or module path
- `touches`: { prNumber, at?, description, lineRange? }[] — in order; description is the analyst's own wording, not a summary
- `coChange`: { path, sharedPrs }[] — files that moved alongside this one
- `maxTouches`: number — cap on rendered nodes; the middle collapses into a stated count, first and last always kept
- `renameCaveat`: string — stated when a git rename may have truncated the history (the corpus does not track renames)
- `staggerMs`: number — total node reveal window (default 1100)

Emphasize target: "touch:<prNumber>" or "pr:<prNumber>", a node by 0-based index, "path" or "cochange".

Example `primitive`:

```json
{
  "template": "file-trajectory",
  "content": {
    "path": "packages/sidecar/src/mcp/server.ts",
    "maxTouches": 9,
    "renameCaveat": "Renames are not tracked in the corpus — touches before any git mv are not represented.",
    "touches": [
      {
        "prNumber": 17,
        "at": "2026-08-05",
        "description": "Stand up the MCP server entry point",
        "lineRange": "L1-L84"
      },
      {
        "prNumber": 18,
        "at": "2026-08-05",
        "description": "Register the first three tool handlers",
        "lineRange": "L84-L162"
      },
      {
        "prNumber": 19,
        "at": "2026-08-06",
        "description": "Thread userId through every handler for tenancy"
      },
      {
        "prNumber": 21,
        "at": "2026-08-07",
        "description": "Wire the corpus query surface into the tool list",
        "lineRange": "L162-L240"
      },
      {
        "prNumber": 22,
        "at": "2026-08-08",
        "description": "Split transport from handler registration for hosting"
      },
      {
        "prNumber": 24,
        "at": "2026-08-09",
        "description": "Return typed errors instead of throwing strings"
      },
      {
        "prNumber": 26,
        "at": "2026-08-10",
        "description": "Refuse unjoinable check inputs at the boundary",
        "lineRange": "L240-L288"
      },
      {
        "prNumber": 30,
        "at": "2026-08-12",
        "description": "Expose the skill surface as a tool"
      },
      {
        "prNumber": 31,
        "at": "2026-08-13",
        "description": "Validate ledger payloads before write",
        "lineRange": "L288-L331"
      },
      {
        "prNumber": 32,
        "at": "2026-08-14",
        "description": "Fix the two defects the clean-machine gate found"
      },
      {
        "prNumber": 33,
        "at": "2026-08-14",
        "description": "Surface snapshot counts through the query tool"
      }
    ],
    "coChange": [
      {"path":"packages/sidecar/src/ledger.ts","sharedPrs":7},
      {"path":"packages/sidecar/src/validate.ts","sharedPrs":5},
      {
        "path": "docs/active_plans/SIDECAR-SURFACE-COMPLETION.md",
        "sharedPrs": 8
      }
    ],
    "staggerMs": 1100
  }
}
```

### objective-ledger

The "what got done" beat of a series explainer: objectives from many PRs rolled into one ledger, grouped by era, each line attributed to its PR and coloured by kind (primary / secondary / constraint). When maxItems truncates the list, the number left out is stated in a row and in the header coverage chip rather than silently dropped.

Content slots:

- `title`: string — optional headline (default "What the work set out to do")
- `groups`: { era, items: { prNumber, statement, kind? }[] }[] — grouped by era
- `showKinds`: ('primary'|'secondary'|'constraint')[] — which kinds to render (default all three)
- `maxItems`: number — cap on rendered rows, spread across groups so no era vanishes; the remainder is disclosed, not hidden
- `staggerMs`: number — total row reveal window (default 1100)

Emphasize target: "pr:<number>", "era:<label>", or a row by flat 0-based index ("item:3" or "3").

```json
            "kind": "primary"
          },
          {
            "prNumber": 15,

            "kind": "primary"
          },
          {
            "prNumber": 16,
            "statement": "Keep templates calm by default",
            "kind": "constraint"
          }
        ]
      },
      {
        "era": "The Sidecar build-out",
        "items": [
          {
            "prNumber": 17,
            "statement": "Stand up the ledger as the doc-state record",
            "kind": "primary"
          },
          {
            "prNumber": 21,
```

### outro-card

Closing slide of a PR-explainer run. Bookends pr-title-card with the same glass plate, brand mark, and footer language. Anchored by an italic takeaway sentence and a colour-coded OBSERVATION chip (Minor Notes / Several Notes / Potential Security Issues). The chip is observational, not a merge recommendation — the agent does not vote on the PR. Optional next-step bullets and a PR# / sha / date footer fill out the card. Optionally lists up to 3 managed planning docs the PR touches, each with a fixed state label.

Content slots:

- `takeaway`: string — one-line, observational, plain language. What the script saw. Italic display. Avoid "approve" / "request changes" framing.
- `observation`: enum — "minor-notes" | "several-notes" | "security-concerns". Drives chip text + colour. Text is fixed per enum; no override.
- `prNumber`: string — "#384" (with or without leading #)
- `headSha`: string — short head sha
- `analysisDate`: string — ISO date or pre-formatted display string
- `brand`: string — bottom-centre wordmark (default "Lenzon")
- `nextSteps`: string[] — 0–3 short observational bullets. NOT a reviewer to-do.
- `docsImpacted`: ImpactedDoc[] — 0–3 planning docs this PR touches, copied verbatim from the payload. { id, title, path, state, match }. state is "needs-update" | "current" | "retired" and match is "named" | "broad"; both label texts are fixed per value, no override. Section is omitted entirely when the list is empty.

Emphasize target: "takeaway", "observation", "nextSteps" or "brand".

Example `primitive`:

```json
{
  "template": "outro-card",
  "content": {
    "takeaway": "A focused security fix that tightens path validation without changing the public upload API.",
    "observation": "security-concerns",
    "prNumber": "#384",
    "headSha": "a3f29c1",
    "analysisDate": "2026-05-25",
    "brand": "Lenzon",
    "nextSteps": [
      "New realpath check lives at path-validator.ts:42",
      "Regression test added under test/upload/"
    ],
    "docsImpacted": [
      {
        "id": "upload-hardening",
        "title": "Upload Path Hardening And Realpath Containment Checks",
        "path": "docs/active_plans/UPLOAD-HARDENING.md",
        "state": "needs-update",
        "match": "named"
      },
      {
        "id": "storage-concept",
        "title": "Storage Concept",
        "path": "docs/concepts/STORAGE-CONCEPT.md",
        "state": "current",
        "match": "broad"
      },
      {
        "id": "legacy-upload-plan",
        "title": "Legacy Upload Plan",
        "path": "docs/archived_plans/LEGACY-UPLOAD.md",
        "state": "retired",
        "match": "named"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Example beat: `{"at":2,"action":{"type":"emphasize","target":"observation"}}`

### plan-title-card

Opening slide of a spec-explainer run — one planning doc rather than a PR. Glass plate anchored by an italic doc title and a large L1/L2/L3 level badge beside the doc id, with org/repo breadcrumb, a grounding pill (sha, date, days since, lane), a status/PRs/files stat strip, a warn-toned drift note that appears on its own for stale or ungrounded docs, and a repo/path footer.

Content slots:

- `repo`: string — repo name (e.g. "Lenzon-Platform")
- `org`: string — owner / organization (e.g. "horizontwo")
- `docId`: string — doc id from frontmatter (e.g. "pipeline-spec")
- `level`: "L1" | "L2" | "L3" — the planning level, rendered as the badge
- `docPath`: string — repo-relative path (e.g. "docs/PIPELINE.md")
- `headline`: string — the doc title, italic display type
- `subtitle`: string — one supporting line of prose
- `kicker`: string — small uppercase label above the headline
- `status`: string — frontmatter status (e.g. "active")
- `groundedAt`: string | null — short sha last verified at; null = never grounded
- `groundedOn`: string — date of the grounding commit
- `daysSinceGrounding`: number — from the digest; omitted means not shown
- `lane`: "fresh" | "stale" | "attestationDrift" | "unevaluated" — as reported
- `prsDelivered`: number — PRs that delivered this doc, from the digest
- `impactFileCount`: number — files under impacts, from the digest
- `driftNote`: string — what moved since grounding, stated plainly
- `generatedAt`: string — ISO date or pre-formatted display string
- `brand`: string — bottom-centre wordmark (default "Lenzon")

Emphasize target: "headline", "badge", "grounding", "stats" or "drift".

Example `primitive`:

```json
{
  "template": "plan-title-card",
  "content": {
    "repo": "Lenzon-Platform",
    "org": "horizontwo",
    "docId": "pipeline-spec",
    "level": "L3",
    "docPath": "docs/PIPELINE.md",
    "headline": "The PR explainer pipeline",
    "subtitle": "How a pull request becomes a script: clone, analyze, produce, render.",
    "kicker": "Spec explainer",
    "status": "active",
    "groundedAt": "05b5f3d",
    "groundedOn": "2026-09-14",
    "daysSinceGrounding": 42,
    "lane": "stale",
    "prsDelivered": 18,
    "impactFileCount": 37,
    "driftNote": "3 merges have touched this spec’s files since it was grounded.",
    "generatedAt": "2026-10-26",
    "brand": "Lenzon"
  }
}
```

Example beat: `{"at":2,"action":{"type":"emphasize","target":"badge"}}`

### pr-objectives

Frames what a PR is trying to do as three visually distinct tiers: 1–2 primary (largest), 0–4 secondary (medium), 0–3 constraints (smaller, dim, 'WON'T' framing). Rows auto-stagger in; later scenes tick them off via emphasize("check:<id>").

Content slots:

- `title`: string — optional headline (default "What this PR is doing")
- `primary`: { id, statement }[] — 1–2, rendered largest
- `secondary`: { id, statement }[] — 0–4, rendered medium
- `constraints`: { id, statement }[] — 0–3, smaller / muted "WON'T" framing
- `staggerMs`: number — between-tier reveal delay (default 400)

Emphasize target: an objective id to pulse it. "reveal:<id>" shows it, "check:<id>" ticks it off and stays, "uncheck:<id>" undoes that.

Example `primitive`:

```json
{
  "template": "pr-objectives",
  "content": {
    "title": "What this PR is doing",
    "primary": [{"id":"obj-1","statement":"Close the symlink escape gap"}],
    "secondary": [
      {
        "id": "obj-2",
        "statement": "Make path validation testable in isolation"
      },
      {"id":"obj-3","statement":"Tighten upload error messages"}
    ],
    "constraints": [
      {"id":"obj-4","statement":"Preserve the public upload API"},
      {"id":"obj-5","statement":"No database migrations"}
    ],
    "staggerMs": 400
  }
}
```

Example beat: `{"at":2,"action":{"type":"emphasize","target":"check:obj-2"}}`

### pr-title-card

Opening slide of a PR-explainer run. Glass plate anchored by an italic PR title and a giant mono PR number, with org/repo breadcrumb, branch rail, additions/deletions/files stat strip, optional label chips, and an author/reviewers/date/sha footer. Visually distinct from title-card.

Content slots:

- `prTitle`: string — the PR headline, italic display type
- `prNumber`: string — "#384" (with or without leading #), giant mono
- `repo`: string — repo name (e.g. "next.js")
- `org`: string — owner / organization (e.g. "vercel")
- `author`: string — PR author handle (e.g. "@ricky")
- `reviewers`: string[] — 0–4 reviewer handles
- `branchFrom`: string — head branch (e.g. "feature/path-validation")
- `branchTo`: string — base branch (e.g. "main")
- `additions`: number — added lines (rendered "+247")
- `deletions`: number — removed lines (rendered "−83")
- `filesChanged`: number — files touched
- `labels`: { text, color? }[] — 0–4 label chips
- `headSha`: string — short head sha
- `analysisDate`: string — ISO date or pre-formatted display string
- `brand`: string — bottom-centre wordmark (default "Lenzon")

Emphasize target: "prTitle", "prNumber", "stats", "labels" or "author".

Example `primitive`:

```json
{
  "template": "pr-title-card",

    "prTitle": "Tighten path validation in the upload handler",
    "prNumber": "#384",
    "repo": "next.js",
    "org": "vercel",
    "author": "@ricky",
    "reviewers": ["@ana","@sam"],
    "branchFrom": "feature/path-validation",
    "branchTo": "main",
    "additions": 247,

  }
}
```

### review-priority-matrix

Reading plan for a series under one lens — a 2×2 of impact × review-worthiness with one dot per PR. The lens (security, correctness, architecture, user-experience, operability, compliance) is required and rendered, since it is what gives the axes meaning. Quadrants are a reading order ("Examine first" / "Read closely" / "Skim" / "Defer"), not a risk verdict. Unscored PRs are stated in the footer rather than omitted. emphasize("quadrant:topRight") lights a whole cell — the "start here" beat.

Content slots:

- `title`: string — optional headline (default "Where to look first")
- `lens`: { id, label, question? } — REQUIRED. id is one of security, correctness, architecture, user-experience, operability, compliance
- `items`: PriorityItem[] — { prNumber, title, impact 0-1, likelihood 0-1, rationale?, era?, files? }
- `unscored`: { prNumber, reason }[] — PRs in the window that could not be scored; rendered as a stated footer
- `xAxis`: { label?, low?, high? } — defaults "Review worthy", "unlikely"/"likely"
- `yAxis`: { label?, low?, high? } — defaults impact under lens, "low"/"high"
- `quadrantLabels`: { topRight?, topLeft?, bottomRight?, bottomLeft? } — defaults Examine first / Read closely / Skim / Defer
- `maxItems`: number — keep the N highest-priority PRs; the remainder is disclosed as a count
- `staggerMs`: number — between-dot reveal delay (default 200)
- `basisNote`: string — override the on-artifact triage disclosure; it cannot be removed

Emphasize target: "quadrant:topRight" (or topLeft, bottomRight, bottomLeft) lights a cell and its dots. "pr:<number>" or a bare number pulses one PR. A "reveal:" prefix shows before it pulses.

Example `primitive`:

```json
{
  "template": "review-priority-matrix",
  "content": {
    "title": "Where to look first",
    "lens": {
      "id": "security",
      "label": "Security",
      "question": "Could this be exploited or leak?"
    },
    "xAxis": {"label":"Review worthy","low":"Unlikely","high":"Likely"},
    "yAxis": {"label":"Impact if wrong","low":"Low","high":"High"},
    "items": [
      {
        "prNumber": 26,
        "title": "Refuse checks with unjoinable inputs",
        "impact": 0.82,
        "likelihood": 0.78,
        "rationale": "Input validation on a path that now rejects rather than returning empty.",
        "era": "packages/sidecar",
        "files": ["packages/sidecar/src/validate.ts"]
      },
      {
        "prNumber": 21,
        "title": "Corpus query surface",
        "impact": 0.88,
        "likelihood": 0.44,
        "rationale": "Tenancy boundary — userId-first, but every new query is a new place to forget it.",
        "era": "packages/sidecar",
        "files": ["apps/server/lib/corpus/queries.ts"]
      },
      {
        "prNumber": 33,
        "title": "Surface the corpus in the UI",
        "impact": 0.61,
        "likelihood": 0.72,
        "rationale": "First externally reachable surface for the indexed data.",
        "era": "apps/server",
        "files": ["apps/server/app","infra/workers"]
      },
      {
        "prNumber": 17,
        "title": "Hosted corpus MCP server",
        "impact": 0.55,
        "likelihood": 0.3,
        "rationale": "Auth is delegated; the token path itself was not touched.",
        "era": "packages/sidecar"
      },
      {
        "prNumber": 12,
        "title": "Entity-map coordinate fixes",
        "impact": 0.14,
        "likelihood": 0.2,
        "rationale": "Rendering geometry only — no data path.",
        "era": "apps/player"
      }
    ],
    "unscored": [{"prNumber":14,"reason":"no analysis"}],
    "staggerMs": 220

}
```

### series-title-card

Opening slide of a series-explainer run — a stretch of work rather than one PR. Glass plate anchored by an italic headline and a mono PR range ("#10 → #33"), with org/repo breadcrumb, date-span pill, PR/day/analyzed stat strip, an optional warn-toned gap note for PRs the corpus could not see, and a repo/window footer.

Content slots:

- `repo`: string — repo name (e.g. "Lenzon-Platform")
- `org`: string — owner / organization (e.g. "horizontwo")
- `prRange`: { from, to } — first and last PR in the window
- `dateRange`: { from, to } — ISO dates or pre-formatted display strings
- `prCount`: number — PRs in the window
- `analyzedCount`: number — PRs with a usable analysis (may be < prCount)
- `dayCount`: number — days spanned; derived from dateRange when omitted
- `headline`: string — the arc in one line, italic display type
- `subtitle`: string — one supporting line of prose
- `kicker`: string — small uppercase label above the headline
- `gapNote`: string — PRs in range with no analysis, stated plainly
- `generatedAt`: string — ISO date or pre-formatted display string
- `brand`: string — bottom-centre wordmark (default "Lenzon")

Emphasize target: "headline", "range", "span", "stats" or "gap".

### title-card

Opening slide of an analysis: a single full-bleed glass plate with a kicker, org/repo display headline, optional blurb, and a meta footer (analysis date, commit · branch). Use it as the first scene of an explainer about one repo.

Content slots:

- `org`: string — owner / organization shown above the repo name
- `repo`: string — repository name, the largest type on the plate
- `blurb`: string — optional 1–3 sentence subtitle below the title
- `kicker`: string — small mono label above the title (default "Codebase analysis")
- `sceneTag`: string — top-right badge text (default "T-00")
- `eyebrow`: string — top-left mono caption (default "§ 00 / title-card")
- `analysisDate`: string — ISO date or pre-formatted display string
- `commit`: string — short commit sha
- `branch`: string — branch name (e.g. "main")
- `brand`: string — bottom centre wordmark (default "Lenzon")

Emphasize target: "repo", "blurb", "kicker", "date" or "commit".

Example `primitive`:

```json
{
  "template": "title-card",
  "content": {
    "org": "vercel",
    "repo": "next.js",
    "blurb": "A walkthrough of the App Router internals — how requests flow through the framework, where caching lives, and why use server changes everything downstream.",
    "kicker": "Codebase analysis",
    "sceneTag": "T-00",
    "eyebrow": "§ 00 / title-card",
    "analysisDate": "2026-04-28",
    "commit": "a3f29c1",
    "branch": "main",
    "brand": "Lenzon"
  }
}
```

Example beat: `{"at":2,"action":{"type":"emphasize","target":"repo"}}`
